title: Benchmarking and Continuous Performance Monitoring of Ookami, an ARM Fujitsu A64FX Testbed Cluster
problem: Frequent software updates in HPC testbed systems make it difficult to detect overall performance degradation, as improvements in some applications can mask performance losses in others. Understanding performance evolution on testbeds like Ookami requires continuous monitoring to separate signal from noise.
motivation: Continuous performance monitoring is critical for maintaining optimal HPC system performance and understanding the true impact of software updates on testbed systems.
method: The authors deployed XDMoD (eXtreme Data Management Optimization and Monitoring Daemon) on Ookami, an ARM-based Fujitsu A64FX HPC testbed with SVE-512 support. Over 3+ years of continuous monitoring, they tracked application and numerical library performance evolution across software releases and analyzed performance improvement patterns.
key_novelty: Long-term empirical quantification of performance evolution on an ARM-based HPC testbed, showing that largest gains occur upon initial technology support release rather than through incremental software optimization.
contributions: Three years of continuous performance monitoring data on Ookami ARM Fujitsu A64FX system using XDMoD
Analysis demonstrating largest performance improvements occur at initial release with new technology support, followed by smaller incremental gains
Empirical observation that vendor-optimized numerical libraries achieve optimization faster than community codes
Evidence of performance masking effects where system-level improvements obscure degradation in specific applications

metrics.other: percentage performance improvements tracked over 3+ years

limitations: Specific quantitative performance metrics and detailed benchmark results are not provided in the abstract.
primary_theme: continuous performance monitoring and software evolution impact
